exposure: treated maternal overt hypothyroidism during pregnancy (TSH > 10 mU/L)
outcome: offspring neurodevelopment (learning and language, neurocognitive development, developmental quotient)
cohort: The study included children born to 31 hypothyroid women with elevated TSH (> 10 mU/L) during pregnancy and 21 euthyroid women with normal TSH levels (0.5-2.5 mU/L) as controls.
finding: Children born to hypothyroid mothers had lower neurocognitive development, particularly in learning and language performance, and were at higher risk of IUGR and reduced 1-min APGAR scores at birth.
mod_finding: Hypothyroid women had a higher prevalence of caesarean sections compared to euthyroid women.
birth_weight: Average birth weight was 2855.6 g for the hypothyroid group's children versus 3285 g for controls.
gest_age: Average gestational age at delivery was 38.2 weeks for hypothyroid women versus 40 weeks for controls.
